summary: This paper proposes a long-range tunable coupler (LTC) based on two quarter-wave CPW resonators coupled via an rf-SQUID to enable tunable interactions between fluxonium qubits separated by over one centimeter for modular quantum processors. The coupler achieves sub-100-ns CZ gates with intrinsic errors below $10^{-4}$ while maintaining low quantum crosstalk and supporting degree-four connectivity for surface codes and higher-degree connectivity for quantum LDPC codes.
motivation: Fluxonium qubits offer long coherence times and high-fidelity gate operations but existing coupling schemes are restricted to close proximity on a single chip, preventing modular architectures needed for large-scale systems while addressing wiring bottlenecks, yield, and crosstalk challenges.
method: The LTC uses two identical $\lambda/4$ CPW resonators (each 0.5 cm long, 50 Ω characteristic impedance) terminated by linear inductors ($L_S = 0.5$ nH) and inductively coupled via a Josephson junction ($I_c = 200$ nA, $E_{J,c}/2\pi \approx 99$ GHz) tuned by external flux bias. Two fluxonium qubits ($E_C/2\pi \approx 1$ GHz, $E_L/2\pi \approx 0.8$ GHz, $E_J/2\pi \approx 6.6$ GHz) couple to the coupler modes with $J_c/2\pi = 125$ MHz; microwave-activated CZ gates exploit the plasmon transition $|1\rangle \leftrightarrow |2\rangle$ with state-dependent frequency shifts $|\delta\omega|/2\pi \approx 64$ MHz.
result: For the one-centimeter coupler, CZ gates via the $|11\rangle \leftrightarrow |21\rangle$ transition achieve 75–100 ns duration with intrinsic error below $10^{-4}$ limited by two-photon transitions; for a longer 1.5 cm coupler with $|\delta\omega|/2\pi \approx 11$ MHz, combining synchronized and DRAG pulse schemes yields sub-100 ns gates with error below $10^{-4}$. Extended analysis shows the LTC can support degree-four surface-code lattices and higher-degree connectivity for LDPC codes with coupling loading manageable via careful capacitor design ($C_{q,L}$ as low as 8–14.5 fF).
